title: Choose one mistake and write what you'd do differently
why_matters: Halfway through your first ninety days, you have enough material to look back on without flinching. Picking one specific moment that didn't go well — and writing what you'd do differently in two sentences, not two paragraphs — is the move that turns a mistake into evidence of judgement. This is the file you'll return to in your probation review.
steps: Look at your private notes from weeks 1-6. Pick one moment where, with hindsight, you'd make a different call. Not the biggest one; one with a clear lesson.
Write three lines: what you did, what you'd do differently, why. Avoid "I should have been more X" — name a specific behaviour, not a personality trait.
File it under "Probation evidence — what I learned".
Move on. Don't ruminate. The writing is the work.
success_criteria: One three-line entry exists in your Probation evidence file. The behaviour change is specific enough that a colleague reading it could spot whether you've done it.
reflection_prompt: What stops you, normally, from naming the mistake — and is that the same thing now?
